hypothesis: Prescribing CAESAR endpoint displacements and rotations to each LFEA source substructure will distinguish local constitutive/load mismatch from errors caused only by the global displacement solution.
predictedSignature: A source whose local formulation matches CAESAR produces CAESAR source-end actions when driven by CAESAR endpoint six-DOF values.
Artificial bend subdivision nodes are eliminated by zero-external-load static condensation rather than prescribed or fitted.
Source 5 can be evaluated only where missing CAESAR source-end actions are uniquely derivable from published incident node actions minus direct neighboring CAESAR source actions.
The replay does not invoke the global LFEA solver and cannot modify production mechanics.
mechanicsDelta: None. Evidence-only instrumentation exposes each already-assembled element global stiffness, equivalent load, and initial-strain load. The replay evaluates q=K*d-f_equivalent-f_initial with CAESAR endpoint DOFs and statically condenses only artificial internal source nodes.
decisionReason: The replay proves the L19 mismatch is local, not merely propagated from wrong global displacements. With CAESAR endpoint DOFs, source 4 still misses L19 FY by about 156.3 N at each end and source 5 by about 192.9 N, while source 4 axial FX differs by only about 0.009 N. Thus the closed-end pressure axial strain on source 4 is essentially correct but transverse frame/bend mechanics remain mismatched. In L20, source 4 develops about 156.6 kN axial replay residual despite identical L19/L20 stiffness, strongly implicating thermal free-strain authority rather than hot-modulus stiffness for that source.
